argv:
Rewrite the text in the house style of The Economist.

Be brief. Be clear. Prefer the short word to the long one, the Anglo-Saxon to
the Latinate, the concrete to the abstract, and the active voice to the
passive. Cut every word that does the work of no word.

Reach for a comparison only if you thought of it yourself; a phrase already
worn smooth by other writers has stopped doing any work. Do not use jargon
when plain English will do, and reach for a Latin or French tag only when no
ordinary English word says the same thing.

State conclusions plainly and with confidence. Dry wit is welcome; whimsy is
not. Do not hedge with "arguably", "it could be said that", or similar
padding.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
Operators must ensure the guard is lowered to within the recommended clearance of the workpiece before the blade is engaged, although the tensioning wheel should be checked periodically throughout a shift regardless of guard position, since drift in tension can occur even when the machine has not been used continuously. The lower blade guide must be inspected for wear whenever the blade has been changed, unless the replacement blade is of the same width and pitch as the one it replaces, in which case a visual check may be sufficient provided the operator has completed the tensioning procedure described elsewhere in this manual. Loose clothing and jewelry should not be worn near the machine, and long hair must be tied back. Operators may leave the work area only after the blade has come to a complete stop, though the machine's residual heat can persist for several minutes and caution is advised.
</passage>

response.text: Lower the guard to the recommended clearance before starting the blade. Check the tensioning wheel every shift regardless of guard position; tension can drift even on machines that sit idle. Inspect the lower blade guide for wear whenever you change the blade. If the new blade matches the old in width and pitch, a visual check will do—provided you have followed the tensioning procedure set out elsewhere in this manual. Wear no loose clothing or jewellery near the machine, and tie back long hair. Do not leave the work area until the blade has stopped completely; even then, the machine stays hot for several minutes, so take care.
